pages.title: Nucleosynthesis
pages.text: $(thing)Nucleosynthesis$()$(br2)Every element heavier than helium was made in a star. Iron is where fusion stops; supernovae make the rest.

$(thing)Insight$(): 90$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Stellar Evolution.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 White Dwarf Core.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Inside a star at temperature T, two nuclei of reduced mass μ must tunnel through their Coulomb barrier to fuse. Their cross-section is S(E)/E times a tunnelling factor exp(−√(E_G/E)). Average the cross-section times relative speed over the thermal distribution of energies E.
